text:
The Dubai residential market recorded 11,608 sales totaling AED 34,328,091,812 in the last four weeks, an 11.4% increase in volume and 25.6% in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations reached 4,630, a separate metric from sales. The off-plan share of transactions stood at 57.2%, down from 65.4% in the previous four weeks.

Median residential pricing rose to AED 1,688 per square foot, a 0.8% increase from AED 1,675. Top sales areas include Dubai South with 3,542 units and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,324 units over twelve weeks. Business Bay showed a 3.5% price decline, while Majan and Dubai Land Residence Complex both posted 1.1% gains.

Rental activity comprised 91,552 contracts with a 51.3% renewal rate. The median residential rent is AED 69,788 annually. Estimated gross yields are highest in Zaabeel First at 8.9% and International City Phase 1 at 8.6%. Town Square, Dubai Sports City, and Dubai Production City follow with yields of 6.9%, 6.7%, and 6.5% respectively.

Price heating is evident in Al Yufrah 1 at 43.3% and Dubai Industrial City at 12.5%. Cooling areas include Liwan at 13.8% and Palm Deira at 13.6%. Anomaly monitoring flagged 1,068 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from comparable medians. Figures reflect registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, portfolio blocks, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
